expectationSemantics: `present` means the item is done and must stay done. `absent` means the item is NOT done and the tree must not quietly acquire it either -- an item that appears without its expectation being flipped is drift in the direction nobody audits. Flipping an expectation is a deliberate edit and shows up in the diff.

items.checkNote: The fix compares the paragraph the action was DISPATCHED on against the paragraph the READ is of, both as fingerprints of the paragraph's own text with the list prefix removed. The prefix removal is load-bearing and measured: the same empty paragraph reads "" before .uno:DefaultBullet and "\u2022 " after it, so a fingerprint over the whole string would differ on every SUCCESSFUL list action and this check would fire on all of them. The two capture points are separate checks because taking either at the wrong moment silently breaks it -- the dispatch one after the dispatch describes a paragraph the action already changed, and the readback one after the restore describes the restore rather than the read. NAMED LIMIT: two paragraphs with the same text are indistinguishable, so an overshoot from one empty paragraph into another is not caught.

items.title: the product prescribes a rollback whose button it does not show -- finding 053, FIXED on shell v9, user-side reachability still unproven
items.source: finding 053; found 2026-08-16 by driving listener:click#notice-action for the first time
items.note: `recoveryFor()` returns "rollback" for any format failure whose barrier says dispatched:true, and the product toasts that prescription; but `#notice`, which carries the button, is displayed only while the session state is `recoverable-error` or `restart-required`, and EDITOR_FORMAT_POSTCONDITION_FAILED puts it in neither -- it is not in RECOVERY_ERRORS. So the user is told the document may have changed unverifiably, and is offered no way back. The error is reachable on the shipped artifact: d2-presweep records it with recovery:"rollback", dispatched:true, in both browsers. WHICH SIDE TO CHANGE IS NOW DECIDED (2026-08-16, external adjudication, verified line by line): SPEC E2-B 5.13 clause three prescribes not merely rollback but that the host ENTER `recoverable-error`, so the shell is out of spec and the page is correct. The fix goes in `NarrowEditorV2Session.action()`'s catch -- compute recoveryFor(error) and call this._blockQueue(error, "recoverable-error", "editor-recovery") before rethrowing -- which touches NOTHING in the E1-C bundle (5 files, none under editor-shell-v2/). It DOES put the E2-C shell bundle from v8 to v9, and D5 round 7 is bound to v8, so it is a planned rebinding and not a slip-in. EXECUTED 2026-08-16: shell v8 -> v9 eb76c5be…, E1-C verified still intact (E1_GO_ODT_EDITOR, failedProperties []), and the seam test goes red without the fix. What is still NOT shown is that a user can reach EDITOR_FORMAT_POSTCONDITION_FAILED through the product page: the product-path route reaches recoverable-error via MUTATION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, which blocked the queue before the fix too.

items.title: the product build never calls setAccessibilityState -- SHIPPED in the second link (d538ce0b); the datum is STILL empty under WASM, which is finding 056
items.note: `refreshEditorAccessibility()` is the only thing that calls setAccessibilityState(..., true), and its single call site sits inside `#ifdef OXSDK_EDITOR_DISCOVERY` AND `#ifndef OXSDK_FINDING_016_SELECTION_BARRIER`. The product profile defines both, so the call is compiled out and getA11yFocusedParagraph() has always returned an empty paragraph there. Found by measurement, not by reading: the first run after the v3 link reported the SAME fingerprint for every paragraph while the caret moved, and that fingerprint was the hash of the empty string. Consequence: the block-identity half of the v3 link -- the barrier comparison and the paragraph in the caret answer -- is INERT on the shipped artifact, and D-BI-2 and D-BI-3 could not have held. The four native rounds this was designed from enabled accessibility themselves, which is the tree's standing lesson (harness path vs product path) landing one level in. Fixed by calling it at document open, where every profile reaches it. SHIPPED 2026-08-17 in artifact d538ce0b: the engine now reports enabled:true, unavailable empty and paragraphFresh true -- and the focused paragraph is STILL empty, with changeCount 0. Native, same sequence, same core commit, is populated at once. That is a platform difference and it is finding 056; this item is done, the datum is not. MECHANISM ESTABLISHED same day, findings/evidence/queue-block-identity/mechanism-of-056/: the call is fine and core cannot honour it. The core build is configured --with-wasm-module=writer, which sets ENABLE_WASM_STRIP_ACCESSIBILITY, which removes 26 objects from sw/source/core/access (measured: 2 objects in the wasm build, 28 native) and makes SwEditWin::CreateAccessible() return {} -- so Window::GetAccessible() is empty and SetLOKAccessibilityState() returns at `if (!xAccessible.is())` without ever attaching a listener. The shipped artifact d538ce0b agrees: zero hits for SwAccessibleMap/Document/Paragraph, 45 for LOKDocumentFocusListener. The reporting half is in the binary, the producing half is not. setAccessibilityState returns void, which is why this was silent.

items.title: answer a click with (paragraph, offset) instead of inferring it from rectangles -- OPEN, engine-side, DESIGNED and measured 2026-08-16
items.note: REWORDED after measurement. The old wording said three ambiguities 'all reduce to the same missing datum -- which BLOCK the caret is in', and that turned out to be half right. Measured natively over three rounds: (a) there IS no block index anywhere in LOK -- the focused-paragraph payload carries content/position/start/end/listPrefixLength and nothing else, and no getCommandValues command supplies one; (b) what does exist, the paragraph's own text, is a FINGERPRINT, not an identity -- two paragraphs with the same text produce a byte-identical payload while the caret rectangle moves; (c) it settles finding 046 on the cells 046 was measured on -- but NOT in general, because the comparison is between two paragraphs' text and `empty-paragraph.odt` ends with two adjacent empty paragraphs whose text is identical -- (the dispatch paragraph read '\u2022 ' and the barrier's .uno:SelectText read '    \u2022 \nBI-AFTER-EMPTY'), and it settles the same-line-different-x case by OFFSET rather than by block; (d) it does NOT settle finding 052's residual, because x is carried on a line and dropped below it (offset 4 on the line, 7 below it, same x) so every click outside the text lands at the same offset -- a real block index would not help either, since the caret genuinely is in the last block. Every one of (a)-(d) is a NATIVE result on core 26.8; whether the shipped WASM engine reports the same offsets and refreshes the a11y payload on the same schedule is owed to a relink round and is not established here. The remedy for (d) is a different shape and comes from the reference implementation rather than from the measurement: make placing the caret a CALL THAT RETURNS (paragraph fingerprint, offset), instead of posting a click and inferring the outcome from a rectangle. Muya (MarkText's editor core) never inverts that mapping -- its cursor IS {offset, block, path} and geometry only ever goes model->pixels. Design and pre-registered predictions: research/DESIGN-2026-08-16-caret-by-block-and-offset.md. BLOCKED 2026-08-17, and NOT on a link. The paragraph datum this design consumes cannot exist in the current core build (finding 056 mechanism), and no configure flag combination in 26.8 can produce one on Emscripten (finding 057: the Make variable and the C++ macro answer to different configure inputs, and --enable-wasm-strip is forced yes for Emscripten at configure.ac:1280, overriding the command line). Unblocking this needs a configure.ac change and a CORE REBUILD, which is the user's call and the user's machine time. The editorPlaceCaretV2 half already shipped and works (38 ms / 251 ms, replacing a 30 s wait); it does not depend on the paragraph datum. Note also that a rebuild buys a TEST, not a feature: adversarial review enumerated further independent runtime conditions past attachRecursive that have never been exercised.
items.checkNote: WRITTEN 2026-08-17, waiting for the link. The old check watched for `caretBlockIndex`, a field for a datum that does not exist in LOK -- so nothing could ever have implemented it and the check was green by construction. These watch the five places the change actually lives: the engine handler, the reply type, the entry point, the EXPORT LIST (an entry point that is not exported is stripped at link time and the symbol is simply absent at run time), and both halves of the worker -- the operation and the PROJECTION, because that projection is an allowlist and adding the engine half without it is how p1-3c's itemCount came to be measured natively and reported nowhere.

items.title: the engine reports enabled:true on a core build where accessibility can never work -- a capability failure wearing the costume of data
items.note: LOK's setAccessibilityState() returns void and silently does nothing when there is no accessible object, so the engine's `enabled: true` / `unavailable: ""` only ever meant 'this call did not throw'. On the shipped build it can never mean more than that, because core was built with ENABLE_WASM_STRIP_ACCESSIBILITY. The observability the second link added asked the right question of the wrong side of the boundary: it reports what WE did, not what core accepted. Remedy is small and compile-time, no new runtime machinery: include <config_wasm_strip.h> in the engine and, when ENABLE_WASM_STRIP_ACCESSIBILITY is 1, report unavailable: "core-built-without-accessibility" instead of enabled: true. Not worth a link on its own -- ride along with the next one. Until then tools/check_core_build_provides.py is the standing guard and it is RED, which is the honest state.

items.title: the long-document wall has been measured -- one canvas for the whole document, and where that stops working
items.note: layoutCanvas sizes a single canvas to the full document and renderDocument repaints it after every edit. Browsers cap canvas dimensions near 32767px, so at MAX_BACKING_WIDTH 2400 an A4 document reaches the cap somewhere around a dozen pages and rendering breaks silently and browser-dependently; below the cap the per-edit repaint cost grows with document length. 'Open a user's own file' is verified for OPENING only -- nothing has ever measured that a realistic document stays editable. The machinery for the fix is already imported: editor-session.js pulls TileScheduler from reader-shell. First step is a measurement, not a fix: add a 20-page cell and find out where it actually breaks. DONE 2026-08-19, and THREE of the guesses in the note above were wrong. (1) 'Browsers cap canvas dimensions near 32767px': measured by bisection on this machine, the cap is 65,535 in both Chrome and Firefox (65,234 for Chrome at 2400px wide). The wall the product hits is at ~32,767, which is therefore a 16-bit limit INSIDE the render path and not the browser's. (2) 'Around a dozen pages': at this viewport it is 33 pages at devicePixelRatio 1 and 17 at 2 -- and the dpr factor is the part that matters, because the same twenty-page document draws at 1x and is blank at 2x. (3) 'The per-edit repaint cost grows with document length': measured essentially flat -- 60 ms at one page, 127 ms at twenty, about 3.6 ms per page. Latency is not the problem here and the pre-registered 1,000 ms threshold was never approached below the wall. What IS the problem is that past the wall the product paints a blank page and says nothing: finding 062, and the two items that carry it are queue-long-document-renders-blank-in-silence and queue-canvas-does-not-follow-a-document-that-grew.
items.checkNote: Present now. The cell is named by its check rather than by the `LONG_DOCUMENT_CELL` placeholder the plan used -- the sentinel names the thing that exists, not the thing that was going to be called that.

items.title: finding 059: core APPLIES the parameterised inline format and reports success:false, and the engine's own predicate reads that as failure -- engine-side, needs a link
items.source: finding 059, measured on the shipped v3 artifact 2026-08-17
items.note: inlineFormatArgument() dispatches .uno:Bold with {"Bold":{"type":"boolean","value":...}} and core rejects it on the shipped WASM build; bold, italic and underline all return LOK_COMMAND_FAILED and put the session into recoverable-error. The list actions use the same parameterised mechanism and still work, so the difference is this slot's argument name or type, not parameters in general. On v2 (before the fix) bold APPLIED and merely ignored `enabled` -- which is finding 045 -- so the fix turned a wrong-direction action into no action at all. BLOCKS the next link because shipping again without resolving it ships a build whose formatting buttons cannot be used. Two candidates, both needing native measurement FIRST: withdraw inlineFormatArgument (back to v2 behaviour, on-only), or find the argument form core accepts. Mechanism deliberately not named (040/048 precedent). MECHANISM ESTABLISHED same day by native control (findings/evidence/059/native/): the parameterised .uno:Bold DOES apply -- marker typed after `value:true` comes back fo:font-weight="bold", after `value:false` comes back normal -- while reporting success:false, wasModified:true. The bare form reports success:true and leaves the text NOT bold. The .uno:DefaultBullet control behaves the same way, which is why the barrier path (which does not gate on success) kept working. So DO NOT withdraw inlineFormatArgument: the fix is correct and the defect is commandResultSucceeded() at probe_engine.cpp:1696 requiring success:true, turned into LOK_COMMAND_FAILED at :2286. CANDIDATE PREDICATES, corrected 2026-08-18: the barrier's readback is the ONLY candidate left. wasModified is out, and by source rather than by measurement -- desktop/source/lib/init.cxx:5517-5518 passes pDocSh->IsModified() as a constructor argument to DispatchResultListener, i.e. captured BEFORE dispatchCommand() runs (the member's own comment at :5073 says 'modified before saving', and :5098 copies it out unchanged). It reports whether the document was already dirty, not whether this command changed anything, so it cannot separate an applied command from a refused one. MEASURED 2026-08-18 (findings/evidence/059/native/predicate/, ten arms, prediction committed first): all four slots apply correctly and all four broadcast .uno:<Slot>=true, so the readback IS available for all of them -- including underline and strikeout, whose absence of a state cache is justified in probe_engine.cpp:4308-4310 by a claim about GetKitUnoCommandList() that core's source contradicts. But the predicate must NOT be 'a broadcast arrived': core broadcasts a state CHANGE, so the value:false arms produced no broadcast at all while doing exactly the right thing. The predicate that survives is the barrier's existing one -- compare observed state against requested state (formatBarrierPostconditionMet, :1189). STILL OWED before this ships: a genuine negative arm. The intended refusal (setViewReadOnly) did not refuse -- core applied the command anyway -- so this round proved the predicate agrees, not that it can disagree. Also unmeasured: whether the state cache is primed when the predicate needs it (finding 021's shape). Superseded note follows: the readback was to be measured PER SLOT: bold, italic, underline and strikethrough are four different slots and the last two have no state cache. A refusal arm must use a command core knows but cannot run -- an unknown slot emits no LOK_CALLBACK_UNO_COMMAND_RESULT at all (comphelper/source/misc/dispatchcommand.cxx:48-50), so it would measure nothing. MEASURED 2026-08-18 (findings/evidence/059/wasm/): the WASM build DOES apply the command while reporting failure, for all four slots -- each arm's marker comes back carrying exactly the slot that was pressed, with a no-command control on the same fixture coming back unstyled. So the shipped product applies the user's formatting and then tells them the action failed and to return to a checkpoint: it asks them to discard work to undo a change that succeeded. That raises the cost of NOT fixing this and it is why this item blocks the link. Also measured: the range route is closed engine-side -- with the page's gesture mask lifted all four dispatches return EDITOR_FORMAT_GESTURE_UNSUPPORTED from editorGesturePermitted (probe_engine.cpp:4247-4252), which is the first RUNTIME witness for p1-2-gesture-mask-inherited. THE TWO THINGS OWED ARE NOW MEASURED (2026-08-19, findings/evidence/059/native/negative-arm/, nine arms, zero disagreements, analyzer self-test 10/10). (1) THE PREDICATE CAN SAY NO, on two arms, and it says no exactly where the document says no: a wrong argument TYPE ({"Bold":{"type":"string",...}}) leaves the text normal with no broadcast, and a paragraph inside a text:protected section refuses the dispatch and does not even take the typing. Asked four ways rather than one, because 037's lesson is that a guard may decline for another reason or not at all -- and setViewReadOnly, asked again, STILL does not refuse. (2) THE CACHE IS PRIMED, at document load, for all four slots including underline and strikeout, which contradicts probe_engine.cpp:4308 a second way (core's own source already did). But the priming comes from the LOAD broadcast, not from caret movement: moving between two paragraphs that share a state broadcasts nothing, so an engine that starts listening later is back in finding 021's shape and the implementation must not assume a gesture refreshes it. (3) NEW, and it sharpens why the current gate is wrong rather than merely weak: `success: true` appeared on exactly the two arms where core IGNORED the argument and toggled, and `success: false` on every arm where core honoured the parameterised form. The field commandResultSucceeded() gates on is ANTI-CORRELATED with the caller's request being honoured on this build. WHAT IS STILL OWED: the engine change itself, and the WASM half of this measurement -- nothing above describes the WASM build (040/048 precedent). THE ENGINE CHANGE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN ON 2026-08-19, and the reason is this finding's own history: 045's fix shipped with native evidence, a static check, a queue item and a link -- and nobody ever pressed the button, which is what 059 IS. Writing a second engine fix that cannot be exercised until the next link repeats that shape exactly. The half that was owed and blocking (the negative arm, the priming) is measured and committed; what remains is unblocked by evidence and gated only on the link, which is the user's decision. THE DESIGN, so whoever links has it: (a) `parseFormatStatePayload`'s booleanCommands list (probe_engine.cpp:1167) carries only Bold/Italic/DefaultBullet/DefaultNumbering -- Underline and Strikeout must be added there and in `updateEditorFormatState` (:1435); (b) the new state fields must go INSIDE the OXSDK_E2_FORMAT_BARRIER guard, NOT beside boldKnown/italicKnown which are unguarded -- the comment at :283 says why, E1-C validated the frozen e1-editor profiles at a specific WASM hash and an unguarded field silently changes what they emit; (c) the gate itself is at :2286, where `!commandResultSucceeded(payload)` becomes LOK_COMMAND_FAILED. For the four inline commands that call must consult the postcondition instead, under the name `inlineFormatArgumentResolved` so this item's sentinel flips visibly. TWO HAZARDS, both measured rather than anticipated: (1) DO NOT gate the inline postcondition on `formatStateStale`. It is set true by every caret move (:2177) and cleared only when a watched payload arrives (:1459) -- and the 2026-08-19 round measured that moving between two paragraphs that already share a state broadcasts NOTHING. So a stale-gated postcondition would refuse exactly the case where the document is already in the requested state, which is a correct outcome, not a failure. (2) The engine's own comment at :423-427 says the state broadcast cannot be the postcondition because core stays silent when nothing changed. That objection is about treating the broadcast as an EVENT and it stands. Comparing the cached STATE against the requested value is a different thing and does not have that problem: 'the command never arrived and the state was already right' and 'the command arrived and set it' both score met, and both are correct -- the postcondition holds either way.
items.checkNote: Absent until the engine carries a resolved form, under a name that did not exist before so the flip is visible in the diff. Deliberately NOT watching `inlineFormatArgument` itself: it is present today and present is exactly the state that is broken.

And both measure the RECOVERY MACHINE rather than the user's route INTO it, so they are a supplement, never a replacement.

items.title: the product tells the user 'there was no checkpoint' when the checkpoint save FAILED -- shell-side, no link needed
items.source: finding 061; measured 2026-08-19 by the checkpoint-write-fails mutation
items.note: editor-shell/recovery-notice.js already decides the difference (`checkpointFailed`: hasCheckpoint false AND checkpointError set) and says in its own comment why -- 'there is nothing to rescue' and 'we tried to protect your work and the save failed' are not the same thing to say to someone. web/e2-editor-app.js does not use that module; its notice branches on `hasCheckpoint` alone, so the failure case prints '沒有檢查點，所以自上次儲存以來的內容不會回來'. The status strip does show 寫入失敗, so the fact is on screen -- in a debug pill, not in the notice that is telling the user what they are about to lose. Measured, not read: with the checkpoint save given a 1 ms deadline the pill reads 寫入失敗 and the notice prints the nothing-to-rescue sentence verbatim.
items.checkNote: Watched by NAME, and the name is not arbitrary: the shell's own module calls this decision `checkpointFailed` (editor-shell/recovery-notice.js), and the honest fix is for the page to take that decision rather than re-deriving a two-way branch from `hasCheckpoint`. A fix written inline under some other name would leave this item reading 'still open' when it is done -- an approximation recorded here rather than hidden, because the alternative sentinel is the notice's WORDING and this queue must not start depending on a sentence nobody has written yet. The first sentinel tried was `checkpointError ?`, which the STATUS PILL already contains: it drifted immediately, which is the checker doing its job.

items.title: finding 062's LAYER is established: the ENGINE returns an unpainted tile above 32,767 px and reports success
items.note: The wall is bracketed narrowly: with one document held fixed and devicePixelRatio swept, 32,590 px of canvas height draws and 32,889 px is blank, and 32,767 = 2^15-1 sits between them. It is NOT the canvas element's cap -- that was measured separately at 65,535 in both Chrome and Firefox, and 65,234 for Chrome at 2400 px wide -- so this is a 16-bit limit inside the render path. The same twenty-page document draws at devicePixelRatio 1 and is blank at 2, so it is a property of the document times the display, not of the document. blocksRelink is FALSE and that is not a judgement that this is unimportant: the first work owed is the experiment that says WHICH LAYER loses the pixels, and until that is done, declaring it engine-side would be the mistake findings 040 and 048 were filed against. THE EXPERIMENT: call document.render() through the shell with canvasHeightPx 32,590 and 32,889 and compare the returned width/height and pixel byte length. render() does not throw today and the product page publishes no session handle, which is why this cannot be answered from the product path. If the engine returns an empty tile this item becomes engine-side and blocksRelink must be flipped. ANSWERED 2026-08-19 (findings/evidence/062/layer/): THE PAGE SIDE, and no link is needed. Asked step by step on the shipped artifact, at heights straddling the wall. The engine's tile is correct at every height -- byte length exactly width x height x 4, dark pixels present, nothing thrown, including at 34,847 where the product is blank on the same document. ImageData builds from all of them. putImageData paints them, on a detached canvas and on one attached and CSS-sized like the product's. And the decisive one: with the PRODUCT sitting in its blank state, a block painted onto that same canvas by the harness lands 36,250 of 36,250 expected pixels while the product's own ink is one column. Same canvas, same size, same moment. So the canvas is fine, the engine is fine, and the product never put the tile there. WHICH page-side step is NOT established and is tracked separately as queue-long-document-blank-page-is-page-side. CORRECTED THE SAME DAY. The paragraph above said page side. It was wrong, and the way it was wrong is the reusable part: every probe run swept an ASCENDING LADDER of canvas heights inside ONE engine session, so the first render was always below the limit and painted, and the later over-limit arms came back carrying content -- which exonerated the engine. One render per page load, which is what the product actually does, returns an unpainted buffer every time. THE ANSWER IS THE ENGINE SIDE and the limit is exactly 2^15-1: at width 362, height 32,767 paints (41,762 dark pixels) and 32,768 does not, at the same 45.2 MB; at width 725, 32,767 paints and 34,847 does not. Two widths, buffers differing by a factor of two, the same height boundary -- so it is the HEIGHT, not the memory. The buffer is always exactly width x height x 4 bytes, ImageData always builds, and render() never throws. The three page-side steps were each measured and are each fine: the product's putImageData paints exactly the all-zero image it is handed (2,105,295 of 2,105,340 sampled pixels fully transparent), its blank canvas takes 36,250 of 36,250 pixels from the harness, and the paint request it sends is byte for byte the one the probe sends. WHY THIS STILL DOES NOT BLOCK THE LINK: nothing forces the product to ask for one tile as tall as the whole document. Rendering in strips no taller than 32,767 -- or using the TileScheduler editor-session.js already imports -- avoids the limit entirely and is a page-side change.
items.checkNote: Present now: finding 062 carries the token. The item is about the LAYER question only; the remaining work is its own item.

items.title: an edit that adds a page leaves the new page undrawn and unmentioned -- page-side, no link needed
items.note: DocumentHandle.heightTwips is assigned once from the open metadata (sdk/document-sdk.js:374) and `document-invalidated` calls renderDocument() and nothing else (web/e2-editor-app.js:622) -- no metadata re-read, no layoutCanvas(). Measured through the product's own buttons: a two-page document opens at a canvas height of 2007, an insert of 3,336 characters leaves it at 2007, and saving those bytes and re-opening them gives 3002 -- which is exactly what a genuine three-page document reports. So the document grew by a page, the canvas did not, and nothing was said. This half has no page-count threshold: it fires at two pages. Fix: re-read the document metadata on invalidation and call layoutCanvas() when the height changed.
items.checkNote: Watched for the shape of the fix at the invalidation handler. Approximate, like the 061 sentinel, and recorded as approximate rather than hidden.

items.title: the product asks the engine for a tile taller than it will paint -- page-side fix, no link needed
items.note: SUPERSEDES the version of this item written on 2026-08-19 before the layer was corrected; that one asked which PAGE-SIDE step dropped the tile, and the premise was wrong -- no page-side step drops it, the engine returns an unpainted buffer above 32,767 px (see queue-long-document-renders-blank-in-silence and finding 062). What is owed is on the page after all, but it is not a bug hunt: layoutCanvas() sizes ONE canvas to the whole document and renderDocument() asks for ONE tile that size, so any document past about 33 pages at devicePixelRatio 1 -- or 17 at 2 -- requests something the engine will not paint. The fix is to stop doing that: render in strips no taller than 32,767, or use the TileScheduler that editor-session.js already imports. No link is needed. AND, separately, the product must not paint a tile it cannot verify: the engine reports success for an unpainted buffer, so a page that trusts the return value has no way to tell. Whatever the fix, it owes the user an error rather than a blank page -- that half is what makes a-long-document-is-drawn-or-the-product-says-it-is-not KNOWN_RED today.
items.checkNote: Watching for the page learning that a tile has a maximum height. Approximate, like the other name sentinels in this file, and recorded as approximate.

blocksRelinkSemantics: An item with blocksRelink true must be AS-DECLARED **and**, if it is declared absent, it is still outstanding work -- so P1 is not complete while it is open. Two items are deliberately false: the WASM heap field was withdrawn after measurement (2026-08-16), and the search-after-reopen wedge is an observation the product does not take today. Without this field the checker would report 'P1 complete' whenever every finished item was finished, which is the exact shape of a check that agrees with whatever it is shown.
externalAdjudication2026_08_16: fable, called as a subagent, refuted the premise that the two remaining blockers cannot be measured before the relink. Verified independently, all three claims: (1) tools/build_e2_discovery_profile.py COPIES the wasm (shutil.copy2, --wasm is an input), so a diagnostic profile can be packaged around the frozen 572035ac bytes -- no engine build, same engine; (2) the frozen wasm already serialises "readback":{"parsed": / "blockCount": / "itemCount": / "html":" and "containment":{"checked": (one occurrence each; "preBlocksObserved": zero, correct -- that is today's unlinked change); (3) all six worker patch anchors match exactly once in the FROZEN dist worker. Consequence: 3b's criterion and the containment ordering are both measurable now, for the price of a Python repackage plus browser rounds. Linking before that measurement would risk a v4, which costs the whole E2-B rerun plus E2-C D0-D5 again.

linkDecision.why: `p1Complete: True` means nothing is BLOCKING the link; it does not mean the link should happen now. Held deliberately so the newly characterised engine defect (queue-selecttext-overshoots-empty-paragraph) has a chance to ride along: it is an engine fix, so it can only ship through a link, and linking today would make it cost a second one.
